CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSERVLET

NEW IN KOLDFUSION 4.5

CFSERVLET runs a Java servlet and writes its response into the page, or stores it in CFSERVLET.Output. In ColdFusion 4.5 the request went to a JRun servlet engine; KoldFusion runs the servlet inside its own Java Virtual Machine, against the Servlet API 2.2 classes in cfx.jar, so 1999-era servlets (JSWDK, JRun, ServletExec) run without a separate servlet engine.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFSERVLET CODE="class_name_of_servlet"
    JRUNPROXY="proxy_server"
    TIMEOUT="seconds"
    WRITEOUTPUT="Yes/No"
    DEBUG="Yes/No">
  <CFSERVLETPARAM ...>
</CFSERVLET>

Attributes

CODE
Required. Class name of the servlet. The class is loaded from the java/classes directory of the installation (and reloaded when the class file changes) or from the Java Class Path.
JRUNPROXY
Optional. Host and port of a JRun proxy, for example "127.0.0.1:8081". Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion runs the servlet itself.
TIMEOUT
Optional. Seconds to wait for the servlet before giving up with an error.
WRITEOUTPUT
Optional, default "Yes". "Yes" writes the servlet's response into the page; "No" only stores it in CFSERVLET.Output.
DEBUG
Optional, default "No". "Yes" logs each call (servlet, status, size, time) to servlet.log.

Usage

The body may contain only CFSERVLETPARAM tags. Parameters given with CFSERVLETPARAM NAME=... VALUE=... (and the page's own URL and form fields) are the servlet's request parameters; variables passed with VARIABLE= are request attributes, and whatever the servlet stores back with setAttribute is copied into the variables after the tag.

After the tag, the CFSERVLET structure contains:

Variable Contents
CFSERVLET.Output The response body
CFSERVLET.HeaderName One entry per response header, such as CFSERVLET["Content-Type"]
CFSERVLET.StatusCode The HTTP status set by the servlet (200 unless it says otherwise)
CFSERVLET.StatusText The matching reason phrase

A servlet's HttpSession lives as long as the visitor's CFML session (with CFAPPLICATION SESSIONMANAGEMENT="Yes") or CFID/CFTOKEN cookies. Servlets are created once, init() is called on first use, and SingleThreadModel is honoured. An exception thrown by the servlet becomes an Application error. Without a Java Virtual Machine, or without cfx.jar, the tag raises an error of type Object.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- HelloServlet ships in java/samples; it counts the visits it is handed by reference --->
<CFPARAM NAME="Visits" DEFAULT="0">
<CFTRY>
  <CFSERVLET CODE="HelloServlet" WRITEOUTPUT="Yes" TIMEOUT="10">
    <CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="name" VALUE="KoldFusion developer">
    <CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="visits" VARIABLE="Visits" TYPE="INT">
  </CFSERVLET>
  <CFOUTPUT>
  <P>The servlet answered with status #CFSERVLET.StatusCode# and Content-Type
  #CFSERVLET["Content-Type"]#, and set Visits to #Visits#.</P>
  </CFOUTPUT>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Any">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
    <TR BGCOLOR="##FFCCCC"><TH COLSPAN=2>The servlet could not run</TH></TR>
    <TR><TD>Message</TD><TD>#CFCATCH.Message#</TD></TR>
    <TR><TD>Detail</TD><TD>#CFCATCH.Detail#</TD></TR>
    </TABLE>
    </CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
